purpose: One or more multiple-choice questions stacked on a single slide.

first_arg.accepts: a single question object, OR an array of question objects (stacked on one slide, each scored independently)

question_object_shape.q: REQUIRED string. The question text. Always rendered as PLAIN TEXT (textContent) — HTML tags typed here show up as literal text, they do NOT render. No allowHTML flag exists for this field.
question_object_shape.code: OPTIONAL string. A separate code block rendered in its own <pre><code> BELOW the question text (q) and ABOVE the options. Plain-text semantics like inside a normal <pre>: write < > & freely, nothing is HTML-parsed here either — this is not a way to inject arbitrary HTML, only to show a code snippet.
question_object_shape.lang: OPTIONAL string, only meaningful if `code` is also set. One of: go | js | html | css | bash | docker | yml | json | generic. Auto-colors the `code` block using the same tokenizer/colors as a manual class="lang-go" block. `generic` only grays out line comments (works for languages without a dedicated tokenizer). Omitting `lang` while `code` is set renders the code block uncolored (plain monospace).
question_object_shape.options: REQUIRED array of exactly 4 strings. Rendered as PLAIN TEXT (textContent) — same as `q`, no HTML parsing, no allowHTML flag.
question_object_shape.correct: REQUIRED integer, 0-based index into `options` for the right answer.
question_object_shape.explain:
REQUIRED string. Shown after the learner answers. Rendered as INNERHTML (real HTML, always — this one field IS HTML-capable by default, unlike q/options/code). Safe to use
, , etc. here; if it contains raw text with < > & that is NOT meant to be a tag, escape it yourself.

first_arg.array_form_example: addQuiz([question1, question2, question3], opts?) — each gets its own independent scoring/reset within the same slide.

opts_object.label: string. Overrides the default slide header text (default header text is "Quiz Checkpoint").
opts_object.note: string, Greek. Short instructional line shown under the header.
opts_object.bg: string, image path. Sets a fixed full-slide background image for this slide via the shared #slide-bg-layer. Omit for no background.
opts_object.overlayAlpha: number 0..1, default 0.5. Dark overlay strength over `bg`, for text legibility.
opts_object.backgroundSize: CSS background-size value: "cover" (fill+crop) | "contain" (fit, may letterbox) | "100% 100%" (stretch/distort) | "100% auto" (fit width, height scales) | "auto" (default, natural size).
opts_object.backgroundPosition: CSS background-position value, default "top left", e.g. "center center".

what_does_NOT_exist_here: There is no opts.allowHTML for addQuiz — q and options[] can never contain real HTML, only explain can (and explain is always HTML, unconditionally).

There is no way to put a code block INSIDE q or inside an option string — the only code-block mechanism for quiz is the separate top-level `code`/`lang` fields on the question object, rendered in a fixed position between q and options.
scoring: Fully automatic. 100 if selected option index === correct, 0 otherwise. A 'Score: N%' badge appears next to the slide's Reset button. Never write score text yourself.

minimal_example.js: addQuiz({ q: "Ποια είναι η σωστή δήλωση μεταβλητής στη Go;", options: ["var x int = 5", "int x = 5", "x: int = 5", "declare x as int = 5"], correct: 0, explain: "Η Go χρησιμοποιεί var όνομα τύπος = τιμή." })

example_with_code_block.js: addQuiz({ q: "Τι θα τυπώσει το παρακάτω πρόγραμμα;", code: "func main() {\n fmt.Println(\"hello\")\n}", lang: "go", options: ["hello", "Hello", "error: undefined fmt", "τίποτα, το πρόγραμμα κολλάει"], correct: 0, explain: "Η fmt.Println τυπώνει το string ακριβώς όπως δόθηκε." })

example_array_form_with_opts.js: addQuiz([q1, q2, q3], { label: "Έλεγχος Κατανόησης", note: "Διάλεξε τη σωστή απάντηση για κάθε ερώτηση.", bg: "./images/quiz-bg.jpg", overlayAlpha: 0.6 })

writing_rules: 4 options, similar length/style — no option should stand out by size or level of detail
correct-answer position (the index) should vary across questions in a deck, not always the same slot
distractors should be plausible/related misconceptions, never eliminable by 'obviously silly' reasoning
include at least one distractor per deck that's deliberately ~5 words longer than the correct answer
explain should be one short sentence/paragraph shown after the answer is revealed
